title: A `require` or `autoload` literal and an `as class<T>` string complete, link and hover as the path or name the compiler reads, and a directory link reveals it in the Explorer
scope:
Completion, links, hover and go-to-definition inside the literals of `require` and `autoload` and inside the string
operand of `as class<T>`, the trigger characters that open those lists, and what the VS Code client does with a link to
a directory. Any other string is not decided here.
dependsOnText:
[0099](0099.md) (the request set, and `documentLink` as a projection of the walk), [0193](0193.md)
(trigger characters answered only where a spelling ends).

summary.headline: Paths complete and link in the editor
summary.body:
Inside the path of a `require`, an `autoload` root or an `autoload discover` glob, the editor lists the
folders and `.nvs` files in the folder the path reaches so far. An `autoload` path lists folders only.
Ctrl+click on an `autoload` root or glob shows its folder in the Explorer. An `autoload` prefix lists the
namespaces your code declares, and its hover shows the folders it maps to. In `'App\User' as class<Model>`,
the string lists the classes that are a `Model`, and ctrl+click opens the class.
